html:
Jean-Bédel Bokassa was a Central African army officer who seized power in a coup on 1 January 1966 and ruled until 1979, from 1976 as self-proclaimed emperor.

A veteran of the French army in the Second World War and Indochina, he ran the country as a personal estate, and named himself president for life. In 1977 he had himself crowned in a lavish ceremony that cost a large share of the state's budget.

In 1979 his troops killed schoolchildren who protested against compulsory uniforms, and France removed him in Operation Barracuda. Gifts of diamonds he had made to the French president Giscard d'Estaing became a scandal in Paris. He returned in 1986, was sentenced to death for murder, and was later released.
